key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2–NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but the erosion resistance at 90° impact remains nearly unchanged.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical coatings, axial-feed HV-APS is a practical route to improve hardness and sliding wear performance without expecting a corresponding gain in high-angle erosion resistance.
method: APS with radial powder injection using a single-electrode A60 torch
HV-APS with axial powder feeding using a three-electrode Axial III torch
Compared microstructure, phase composition, microhardness, erosion, and ball-on-disc wear
evidence_signal: HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16%, increased hardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, and lowered wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3, while erosion stayed almost the same (0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g).
watch_item: The improved density and tribological performance do not translate to better erosion resistance under 90° impact, so application-specific validation is still required.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
